summary: Legacy bus-powered USB 1.1 4-in/4-out DJ audio interface from M-Audio, bundled with Torq DJ software and timecode vinyl; no maintained driver for Windows 10/11.
identityNotes: The user calls it 'Torq 4x4'. No product with that name exists; the Torq Conectiv (4 RCA in / 4 RCA out, USB 1.1, 16-bit/48 kHz) is the most plausible match. Alternative: the M-Audio Torq Xponent controller (built-in multichannel interface) or Torq Mixlab, less likely. Recorded as ambiguity; confirm the label on the unit.

documents.title: M-Audio Conectiv driver listing 5.10.0.x
documents.notes: Third-party mirror; no official Windows 10/11 support.

usb.notes: USB 1.1; M-Audio vendor ID 0x0763 (general knowledge); product ID unconfirmed. Not class compliant; requires M-Audio driver.

tests.title: USB 1.1 enumeration and port
tests.why: USB 1.1 interfaces misbehave on some USB 3 controllers; use a different port or a USB 2.0 hub if no audio.
steps: Plug into a USB port directly.
If not detected, try a USB 2.0 port or powered hub.

tests.title: Signal health: Input 1/2 LINE
tests.why: Verifies each input pair and the line/phono switch.
steps: Set the input switch to LINE.
Play a source into the pair and run the test.

tests.title: Signal health: Input 1/2 PHONO
tests.why: Verifies each input pair and the line/phono switch.
steps: Set the input switch to PHONO.
Play a source into the pair and run the test.

tests.title: Signal health: Input 3/4 LINE
tests.why: Verifies each input pair and the line/phono switch.
steps: Set the input switch to LINE.
Play a source into the pair and run the test.

tests.title: Signal health: Input 3/4 PHONO
tests.why: Verifies each input pair and the line/phono switch.
steps: Set the input switch to PHONO.
Play a source into the pair and run the test.

tests.title: Signal health: Output 1/2
steps: Loop the output into a line input of a second interface, or into a mixer and record.
Play a tone and check L/R.

tests.title: Signal health: Output 3/4
steps: Loop the output into a line input of a second interface, or into a mixer and record.
Play a tone and check L/R.

tests.title: Mix knobs and headphone cue
tests.why: The Conectiv blends input and computer audio with MIX knobs and a headphone section.
steps: Sweep each MIX knob fully: smooth transition between input and computer signal.
Check the headphone volume and cue/split controls; the TRS headphone jack.
Test the mic input with a dynamic mic.

tests.title: Hum on phono inputs
steps: Connect a turntable with ground wire, run the test.

tests.title: Phono channel separation
steps: Play L/R separation bands.

tests.title: Timecode check via Conectiv (Torq / Traktor / Mixxx)
tests.why: Check timecode decode through the legacy 16-bit/48 kHz converters.
steps: Play control vinyl via phono input and run the check.
If you only own Traktor media, the Traktor Scratch MK1 format can be tried (compatibility unconfirmed).

tests.title: DVS signal
steps: Play any control vinyl or CD.

tests.title: Latency / buffer
tests.why: Legacy ASIO at 48 kHz: check what buffer works without clicks.
steps: Set ASIO buffer to 256 samples; increase if clicks.

tests.title: Jacks and knobs
steps: Wiggle RCA plugs, rotate knobs, check USB socket.
